stimulus.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Lichen species Arborus flavens and Arborus cinereus both grow on granite outcrops in the Wrenvale region.
• In a 12-week drought simulation, Arborus flavens retained 84% of its photosynthetic activity.
• Under identical conditions, Arborus cinereus retained only 19% of its photosynthetic activity.
• Researcher Elena Voss published the study in 2019 with funding from a regional conservation trust.
• Arborus flavens is used locally as a natural dye source.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the difference in drought resilience between the two lichen species. Which choice most effectively uses the relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: The drought simulation revealed a stark contrast between the two lichens: Arborus flavens retained 84% of its photosynthetic activity, while Arborus cinereus retained only 29%.

Although both lichens grow on the same granite outcrops in the Wrenvale region, they responded very differently to drought: Arborus flavens retained 84% of its photosynthetic activity, whereas Arborus cinereus retained only 19%.
Elena Voss published her study of Wrenvale lichens in 2019 with funding from a regional conservation trust; one of the species she examined, Arborus flavens, is used locally as a natural dye source.
In a 12-week drought simulation, Arborus flavens retained 84% of its photosynthetic activity, and Arborus cinereus retained 19% of its photosynthetic activity.

rationale: The goal is to emphasize a difference, so the sentence must do more than mention the two species — it must perform a contrast using the two decisive figures (84% versus 19% retained photosynthetic activity). Choice B does exactly this: it selects only the goal-relevant notes, states both figures verbatim, and frames them with an explicit contrast ('Although ... whereas ... only 19%'). Choice D uses the right facts but merely lists them side by side with the neutral connector 'and'; the reader must infer the difference, so the rhetorical move the goal requires is never made — a structure mismatch. Choice C is entirely accurate but draws on the publication-funding and dye-source notes, which say nothing about drought resilience — the right facts for the wrong job. Choice A performs the correct contrastive move but corrupts the decisive note, inflating Arborus cinereus's figure from 19% to 29% — a subtle fact distortion that makes the sentence inaccurate even though its rhetoric looks right.
